sections.heading: Hesiod's Shield of Heracles
paragraphs: This is Hugh G. Evelyn-White's 1914 prose translation of the Shield of Heracles, an archaic epic narrating Heracles' battle with Cycnus and centred on an extended description of his shield. The poem is traditionally, though doubtfully, attributed to Hesiod; it is transmitted with the rest of the Hesiodic corpus and is included here on that traditional footing.

The translation is reproduced verbatim; nothing is modernised, abridged or silently corrected. Evelyn-White's own explanatory footnotes are not part of the poem's text and are not reproduced here (see "Known gaps & anomalies").

sections.heading: The edition
paragraphs: Hugh G. Evelyn-White, ed. and trans., Hesiod, the Homeric Hymns and Homerica (Loeb Classical Library, London: William Heinemann Ltd. / New York: The Macmillan Co., 1914). This is the edition that Perseus's TEI transcription of both the Greek text and the English translation of "Shield of Heracles" (Ἀσπὶς Ἡρακλέους) is built from.

Citation in this reader follows the Loeb "card" pagination unit that both language witnesses in the source TEI share (a card typically spans 20–40 lines); Hesiod's poems carry no Book-level division in the manuscript or print tradition, so there is no higher citation level to use instead.

sections.heading: Digital source
paragraphs: The machine-readable text is the TEI XML file tlg0020.tlg003.perseus-eng2.xml (CTS URN urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0020.tlg003.perseus-eng2) from the Perseus Digital Library / OpenGreekAndLatin `canonical-greekLit` GitHub repository. It was fetched once and is bundled with the app; nothing is loaded from the network at runtime.

sections.heading: How it was imported
paragraphs:
The importer walks the single translation
as one continuous text stream and cuts it into 13 cards at each marker (there is no

structure to slice on - see "Known gaps & anomalies"). Evelyn-White's own footnotes () are dropped; wrapping is unwrapped, keeping the word. Entities are decoded and runs of whitespace collapsed; the words are otherwise untouched.

sections.heading: Reference scheme
paragraphs: Citation here is by card, matching the companion shield-of-heracles-grc Greek work card for card. Each card's Division.ref gives the underlying Greek verse line range. Passage.n is "" throughout.

sections.heading: Known gaps & anomalies
paragraphs:
6 translator's footnote(s) were dropped (not the poem's text). No

paragraph structure exists in the source, so each card is imported as a single continuous prose block.
